# ICP / Persona Draft — ICP-001: The Bengali-Mandated Knowledge Publisher

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Artifact ID | ICP-001 |
| Flow Step | 04 — Define ICP / target customer (Phase: Problem Discovery) |
| Owner | PM-001 |
| Upstream inputs | PS-001 (Problem Statement v3.0), IOH-001 (v1.0), IB-001 (v1.0) |
| Reviewers this run | UXR-001 (independent), CMO-001/PMM-001, CRO-001 |
| Version | 1.0 |
| Status | Draft → for independent review |
| Overall confidence | **Medium** (the segmentation logic and the qualification test are strong; every population and price figure is an unverified ESTIMATE) |
| Evidence quality | **Low** — no web research, no CRM, no interviews conducted in this run |
| Gate criteria | **MET** — a narrow, *countable*, and *falsifiable* initial segment is defined in §2, with disqualifiers (§8), a screening instrument (§11) and pre-registered revision triggers (§10) |

---

## 0. What this artifact must do, and what it deliberately does not do

PS-001 concluded that the blockage is **70% not price** (P2 unquantifiable return + P3 unverifiable quality + P4 no route to reader) and named the primary problem-holder as the *reach-motivated institutional content owner*. That is a problem-holder **class**, not a targetable segment: you cannot build a contact list from it, and Step 05 cannot recruit interviewees from it.

This step's only real job is to convert that class into something with three properties:

1. **Countable** — I can, in principle, enumerate the members.
2. **Reachable** — I can find and contact a named individual inside one.
3. **Falsifiable** — membership is decided by observable facts, not by my judgement of their motives.

Everything below is built to satisfy those three. I am **not** writing a full journey (Step 17), messaging (Step 10), or MVP scope (Step 21–22), and I flag one place where this ICP will put pressure on MVP scope (§12) without resolving it here.

---

## 1. The core targeting insight

**INFERENCE — the qualification test that makes this ICP testable:**

> The problem in PS-001 is observable as an **absence**. An organization that (a) publishes English-language long-form content, (b) has a named Bangladesh or West Bengal audience, and (c) has *not* produced a Bengali edition of its flagship content in the last 24 months, **is by definition an instance of the problem** — the mandate exists, the content exists, the Bengali edition does not.

This is worth more than any demographic filter. It means every qualified prospect is *simultaneously* a sales target and a data point, and it means a prospect who has already produced a Bengali edition is not a lead — they are a **control-group interview** telling us how the problem gets solved today (§11.3). No other segmentation available to us has that property.

**Corollary (DECISION D-005, PM-001, autonomous):** "Has a Bengali audience mandate" is **never** self-reported in qualification. It must be evidenced by an observable artifact — a country programme page, a Bangladesh office, a grant with a Bangladesh geography, or a Bengali-language item already on their site. Self-report is unreliable and will inflate the funnel with polite interest.

---

## 2. The beachhead ICP (narrow form)

**DECISION D-006 (PM-001, autonomous, Level 2 in a human-run org):** The initial customer segment is a **single** beachhead, not a portfolio. Two adjacent segments are carried as cheap parallel probes only.

> **BEACHHEAD ICP:** An **international NGO, foundation, global-health/literacy programme, or open-education body**, headquartered outside South Asia and funded in USD/GBP/EUR, that **publishes its own long-form English knowledge products** (guides, handbooks, manuals, training curricula, flagship reports, field books — 25,000+ words), operates a **named Bangladesh or West Bengal programme**, employs at least one dedicated **communications / knowledge-management** person, and has **no Bengali edition** of its flagship title.

Compressed to a sentence a salesperson can hold:

> *"HQ-funded international organisations that write book-length English guidance for a Bangladesh audience they have never translated for."*

### 2.1 Qualification rubric

Used for both interview recruitment (Step 05) and outbound targeting (Step 09). A prospect is **Qualified** only at ≥80 points **and** zero disqualifiers.

| # | Criterion | Type | Points | How it is observed |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Q1 | Owns copyright in its own English long-form content (≥25k words), published in last 36 months | **Must** | 25 | Publication visible on their site/repository |
| Q2 | Named Bangladesh **or** West Bengal programme, office, cohort or grant | **Must** | 25 | Country page, office listing, grant record, partner list |
| Q3 | No Bengali edition of that content exists | **Must** | 20 | Absence of Bengali file/version on their publication page |
| Q4 | Budget denominated and disbursed in USD/GBP/EUR | **Must** | 15 | HQ location + funder currency |
| Q5 | ≥1 named comms / knowledge-management / publications staff member | Should | 10 | Staff page, LinkedIn-equivalent, report colophon |
| Q6 | Existing translation behaviour in *other* languages (French, Spanish, Arabic, Swahili editions exist) | Should | 5 | Multiple language versions on the same publication page |

**Q6 is the highest-signal "should" and is deliberately not a "must".** An org that already ships French and Spanish editions has (i) proven budget for translation, (ii) an internal precedent to point at, and (iii) an *obvious, embarrassing gap* where Bengali should be. **RECOMMENDATION:** rank the Step 05 recruitment and Step 09 outbound list by Q6 first. This is the cheapest available proxy for willingness to pay and it directly de-risks IOH-001's kill trigger K2.

### 2.2 Secondary probes (interview-only this phase, ≤6 of 24 slots)

| Probe | Who | Why probed, not pursued | Slots |
|---|---|---|---|
| **S1 — Faith & mission publishers** | Organisations producing devotional, educational, or scriptural long-form material with an explicit Bengali-reader mission | Structurally the *most* motivated buyer of Bengali reach in existence, owns its own rights, historically funds translation, immune to ROI logic (P2 dissolves). Not the beachhead because doctrinal/theological review adds an unknown QA layer and the category carries positioning and partner-risk we have not assessed | 3 |
| **S2 — Institutional learning-content owners** (EdTech, corporate L&D, courseware, MOOC providers) | IOH-001's H3. Same pipeline, larger recurring wallet, procurement-driven budget | Kept as a probe because it may prove the bigger business (IOH §3.3). Not the beachhead: longer sales cycle, different unit (course ≠ book), likely different quality bar | 3 |

---

## 3. The primary use case (one, specific)

> **Trigger:** A programme is producing or has just published a flagship English knowledge product, and the Bangladesh/West Bengal audience is named in the dissemination plan, the log-frame, or the donor's reporting requirements.
>
> **Job to be done:** *"Get this in front of our Bengali audience within this programme cycle, in language our Dhaka colleagues will endorse rather than correct, and give me something I can put in the donor report proving it landed."*
>
> **Success as the customer defines it:** the Bengali edition exists, the country office signed off on it without a rewrite, it is downloadable/obtainable by the intended readers, and there is a number (downloads, distributed copies, sessions delivered from it) to cite.

### 3.1 Secondary use cases (in scope, lower priority)

| # | Use case | Trigger |
|---|---|---|
| U2 | **End-of-grant dissemination push** | Grant closing in 60–120 days with unspent dissemination line and a "local language" commitment in the log-frame |
| U3 | **Back-catalogue localisation** | New Bangladesh programme starts; 3–8 existing English titles must be made usable locally — *this is the multi-title order and the repeat-business path (IOH kill trigger K5)* |
| U4 | **Proposal differentiator** | Org is bidding for Bangladesh funding and wants "materials available in Bangla" as a credibility line in the proposal |

**INFERENCE:** U3 and U4 matter disproportionately. U1 alone is a one-title purchase and fails K5 (no repeat). U3 is intrinsically multi-title; U4 recurs every funding round. **If discovery finds U3/U4 are real, the offer should be shaped around a catalogue programme, not a single title.**

---

## 4. Persona A (primary buyer / champion) — "Claire M., Knowledge & Communications Lead"

| Attribute | Detail |
|---|---|
| Role titles | Knowledge Management Lead · Communications Manager · Publications Officer · Dissemination Lead · Head of Programme Communications |
| Sits in | HQ (London, Geneva, DC, Amsterdam, Nairobi-as-hub, Copenhagen) |
| Org size | 50–2,000 staff; annual budget **ESTIMATE $5M–$500M** |
| Reports to | Director of Programmes / Director of Communications |
| Owns | The dissemination plan and, usually, a discretionary dissemination/translation line |
| Speaks Bengali | **No.** This is the defining fact about her. |
| Measured on | Publications shipped on schedule; downloads/reach reported to funders; "materials available in local languages" commitments met; **no incidents** |
| Buying authority | **ESTIMATE:** can single-source up to ~$5,000 on a purchase order; above that triggers three quotes or tender (§6) |

### 4.1 Her pains, mapped to PS-001 root causes

| PS-001 cause | How it shows up for Claire | Her current coping behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| **P3 — unverifiable quality** | She cannot read the deliverable. If Dhaka says "this is stiff/wrong register/West Bengal Bangla, not ours," she has personally wasted budget and looks careless in front of a country director | Send it to the country office for review — which converts a 3-week job into a 3-month one, or kills it |
| **P2 — unquantifiable return** | Asked "how many people will read the Bengali version?", she has no number. Cannot defend the line item against competing spend | Defer to "next cycle." Indefinitely |
| **P4 — no route to reader** | She can host a PDF. She cannot get it to a field worker in Rangpur | Publish the PDF on the website and call it done — knowing it is not |
| **P5 — coordination cost** | 5–7 vendors, one unfamiliar language, no way to judge any of them | Ask the country office to "handle it," pushing cost and delay onto colleagues with no capacity |
| **P1 — price** | Real but secondary. Her problem is **defensibility of spend**, not absolute cost | — |

### 4.2 What she must believe before she buys

1. Someone Bengali-speaking and credible **whose name is on it** stands behind the language.
2. Her Dhaka colleague will approve it **without a rewrite** — and ideally is built into the process rather than ambushed by it.
3. There will be **a number** at the end she can put in a report.
4. It fits inside **one purchase order** and **this cycle's** calendar.

**INFERENCE:** Items 1–3 are product/process requirements, not marketing claims. This ICP is quietly specifying an offer that includes a named native reviewer, a country-office sign-off step, and a measurement artifact. That is a materially different product from "cheap fast translation."

### 4.3 What kills the deal for her

- Any hint she must personally judge Bengali quality.
- A price above her single-source threshold.
- A process that requires the country office to do *work* rather than *approve*.
- A timeline that lands after the grant/report deadline.
- Any ambiguity about who owns the resulting Bengali text.

---

## 5. Persona B (the veto) — "Rezaul H., Country Communications Officer, Dhaka"

**The most under-modelled actor in IB-001 and IOH-001, and in my judgement the true gatekeeper.**

| Attribute | Detail |
|---|---|
| Role | Country comms / programme officer / national technical advisor, Dhaka or Kolkata |
| Native Bengali | Yes — he is the only person in the transaction who can actually evaluate the product |
| Formal authority | Usually none over the budget |
| **Real authority** | **Absolute veto.** One email saying "the Bangla is not good" ends the project and the vendor relationship |
| Incentives | Protect the org's local credibility; avoid extra work; avoid being handed a HQ decision as a fait accompli |
| Latent threat to us | He may say *"just give me the budget, my team can do this locally"* — the country-office substitution risk flagged in PS-001 §2 |

**DECISION D-007 (PM-001, autonomous):** Persona B is designated a **first-class user of the product, not a stakeholder to be managed.** Any solution concept (Step 18) that does not give Rezaul a defined, low-effort, high-status role — reviewer of record, named endorser, terminology authority — will be rejected at Step 21 scoping. Rationale: he is simultaneously the only credible quality signal available to Claire (dissolves P3) and the single most likely source of a lost deal. Converting the veto into the guarantee is the highest-leverage design move visible at this stage. *Confidence: Medium-High on the logic; the substitution risk is untested.*

---
